symbols.name: MN
symbols.role: implemented treatment-arm staffing, proved interior for \(N\ge N_0\)

symbols.name: Q0N
symbols.def: \((\mathcal A_{0,N}g)(k)=\lambda(N-k)[g(k+1)-g(k)]+\tau k[g(k-1)-g(k)]\), with unavailable boundary jumps omitted

symbols.name: Q1N
symbols.def: \((\mathcal A_{1,N}g)(k)=\lambda(N-k)[g(k+1)-g(k)]+[\tau k+\nu\min\{k,M_N\}][g(k-1)-g(k)]\), with unavailable boundary jumps omitted

symbols.name: pigamma
symbols.def: \(\pi_\gamma(x)=Z_\gamma^{-1}\exp[-Dx^2/(2q)]\) for \(x\le\gamma\), and \(\pi_\gamma(x)=Z_\gamma^{-1}\exp[-dx^2/(2q)-\nu\gamma x/q+\nu\gamma^2/(2q)]\) for \(x>\gamma\), where \(Z_\gamma\) normalizes the density

symbols.name: hgamma
symbols.def: \(h_\gamma\) is the \(\pi_\gamma\)-centered solution of \(-\mathcal L_\gamma h_\gamma=x-m_\gamma\)

symbols.name: Clambda
symbols.def: \(C_\lambda\) is the pooled number of undesirable-state entries in both arms on \([0,T_N]\)

symbols.name: Ctau
symbols.def: \(C_\tau\) is the pooled number of marked natural recoveries in both arms on \([0,T_N]\)

symbols.name: Cnu
symbols.def: \(C_\nu\) is the number of marked service recoveries in the treatment arm on \([0,T_N]\)

symbols.name: AaN
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_{\ell,N}=\mathcal A_{0,N}\) for \(\ell=0\) and \(\mathcal A_{\ell,N}=\mathcal A_{1,N}\) for \(\ell=1\)

symbols.name: V0N
symbols.def: \(V_{0,N}\) is the exact stationary Poisson energy for \(x-\mathbb E_{\rho_{0,N}}X_{0,N}\) under \((G_{0,N},\rho_{0,N})\)

symbols.name: V1N
symbols.def: \(V_{1,N}\) is the exact stationary Poisson energy for \(x-\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}X_{1,N}\) under \((G_{1,N},\rho_{1,N})\)

symbols.name: h1N
symbols.type: lattice restriction of the diffusion Poisson solution
symbols.def: \(h_{1,N}(x)=h_{p,\gamma_N}(x)\) for \(x\in E_{1,N}\); its lift to counts is \(k\mapsto h_{1,N}(s_{1,N}(k))\)

symbols.name: X0
symbols.def: \(X_0\) is the stationary diffusion with generator \(\mathcal L_0\) and invariant density \(\pi_0\)

symbols.name: Xgamma
symbols.def: \(X_\gamma\) is the stationary diffusion with generator \(\mathcal L_\gamma\) and invariant density \(\pi_\gamma\)

symbols.name: inputname
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak r(m)=\prod_j[r^-_j(m),r^+_j(m)]\) has rational endpoints, contains \(p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G\), is nested in \(m\), and has maximum width at most \(2^{-m}\)

symbols.name: LJ
symbols.role: certified Lipschitz bound returned by the interval oracle

symbols.name: certcover
symbols.type: finite family of rational dyadic intervals
symbols.role: unpruned cover in the capacity certificate

symbols.name: Rloc
symbols.role: fixed compact-state radius in generator convergence

symbols.name: Kres
symbols.role: compact-uniform residual constant sought in Open-ended Question 1

novel.justification: Repeated marked monitoring over a growing trial horizon is natural for adherence services that generate daily or continuous event histories.

assumptions.condition: Every observed recovery jump is labeled as natural or service-induced.

novel.justification: Digital adherence platforms routinely log whether recovery followed ordinary self-verification or recorded sponsor outreach, so the mark is an operational event field rather than an oracle quantity.
A positive staffing shadow price represents the actual resource cost of adding sponsor capacity in a service experiment.
A positive information shadow price represents the planning value placed on shorter inferential intervals.
The explicit enrollment threshold guarantees that the critically scaled integer capacity is positive and below the finite population throughout the maintained rate and staffing boxes.

The fitted-center regime describes operational panels whose monitoring duration grows more slowly than enrollment; this is exactly the relation that makes an order \(N^{-1}\) diffusion-centering error negligible at the \(\sqrt{NT_N}\) inference scale.

definitions.name: piecewise diffusion Poisson construction
definitions.construction: Set \(F_0(x)=\int_{-\infty}^xu\pi_0(u)\,du\) and \(h_0'(x)=-F_0(x)/(q_0\pi_0(x))\). Set \(F_\gamma(x)=\int_{-\infty}^x(u-m_\gamma)\pi_\gamma(u)\,du\) and \(h_\gamma'(x)=-F_\gamma(x)/(q\pi_\gamma(x))\). Choose each additive constant so its solution has stationary mean zero.

definitions.name: kink-residual proof handle
definitions.construction: Restrict the piecewise-Gaussian solution to \(h_{1,N}\) on \(E_{1,N}\), split Taylor's integral remainder according to whether a lattice jump crosses \(\gamma_N\), and combine the exact product ratio \(\rho_{1,N}(k+1)/\rho_{1,N}(k)\) with compact-uniform polynomial tails.

definitions.name: marked exposure-rate estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat p=(C_\lambda/E_\lambda,C_\tau/E_\tau,C_\nu/E_\nu)^{\mathsf T}\), evaluated inside \([c/2,2C]^3\) for plug-in calculations and assigned fixed positive fallbacks when an exposure is zero.

definitions.name: fixed-staffing fitted diffusion center
definitions.construction: Hold the observed \(M_N\) fixed, compute \(\widehat\gamma_N=(M_N-Na(\widehat p))/\sqrt N\), and set \(\widetilde\theta_N=a_0(\widehat p)-a(\widehat p)-N^{-1/2}m_{\widehat p,\widehat\gamma_N}\).

definitions.name: empirical and fitted-center Wald intervals
definitions.construction: \(I_{\mathrm{emp}}=[\widehat\theta_N\pm z_\alpha\sqrt{\widehat V/(NT_N)}]\) and \(I_{\mathrm{fit}}=[\widetilde\theta_N\pm z_\alpha\sqrt{\widehat Q/(NT_N)}]\), where \(\widehat V\) and \(\widehat Q\) plug \((\widehat p,\widehat\gamma_N)\) into \(V\) and \(Q\).

definitions.name: validated capacity-search handle
definitions.construction: Apply the rational interval oracle to a fair dyadic branch-and-bound tree on \([-G,G]\). At depth \(d\), bisect every surviving interval, evaluate it at precision at least \(m_\epsilon+d\), retain a rational incumbent upper bound, and prune only boxes whose certified lower bound exceeds that incumbent. Stop no later than depth \(D_\epsilon\) after the full-level fallback partition has objective gap at most \(\epsilon\).

definitions.name: scaled state, lattice, and prelimit generator
lattice restriction of the treatment diffusion Poisson solution
definitions.construction: Set \(h_{1,N}=h_{p,\gamma_N}|_{E_{1,N}}\); equivalently, its count-lattice lift is \(k\mapsto h_{p,\gamma_N}((k-Na(p))/\sqrt N)\).

definitions.name: rational interval representation of design inputs
definitions.construction: At request \(m\in\mathbb N\), return the nested rational box \(\mathfrak r(m)=\prod_j[r^-_j(m),r^+_j(m)]\) containing \((p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G)\), with maximum coordinate width at most \(2^{-m}\), preserving positive lower bounds for the rate and cost coordinates, \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(G\ge0\).

definitions.name: validated Gaussian and objective interval oracle
definitions.construction: For a rational staffing interval \(I\subseteq[-G,G]\) and precision \(m\), complete squares on both sides of the moving kink and enclose \(\exp\), \(\operatorname{erf}\), and \(\Phi^{-1}\) by rational range-reduced series with signed remainder bounds. Choose rational \(R>|x^*|\), where \(x^*=0\) for \(\gamma\ge0\) and \(x^*=-\nu\gamma/d\) otherwise, and outward-round \(B_R=\sqrt{D/(2\pi q)}\{2q/[d(R-|x^*|)]\}\exp[-d(R-|x^*|)^2/(2q)]\) until both \(B_R\) and \((2q/d^2)B_R\) are at most \(2^{-(m+4)}\). These quantities enclose the omitted stationary probability and Poisson-energy tails. Split validated quadrature at \(\gamma\) on \([-R,R]\). Return \(\mathfrak O(I,m)=[\underline J(I,m),\overline J(I,m)]\) and \(L_J\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) such that \(J(p,\eta)\in\mathfrak O(I,m)\) for every \(\eta\in I\) and \(\overline J-\underline J\le L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+2^{-m}\); point intervals have width at most \(2^{-m}\).

definitions.name: checkable global capacity certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathrm{Cert}=(\gamma_\epsilon,L_\epsilon,U_\epsilon,\{(I_r,\underline J_r,\overline J_r,m_r,\sigma_r)\}_{r=1}^R)\), with \(\sigma_r\in\{\mathrm{active},\mathrm{pruned}\}\), is a rational dyadic partition record. Each oracle receipt encloses \(J\) on \(I_r\); every pruned record satisfies \(\underline J_r>U_\epsilon\); the active intervals cover every global minimizer; the incumbent point receipt at \(\gamma_\epsilon\) has upper endpoint \(U_\epsilon\); and \(L_\epsilon=\min_{r:\sigma_r=\mathrm{active}}\underline J_r\) satisfies \(U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon\le\epsilon\).

statements.statement: Let \(\beta=\min\{c/(3C),2c/(C+2c)\}\) and \(N_0=\left\lceil\{(G+\sqrt{G^2+4\beta})/(2\beta)\}^2\right\rceil\). Uniformly for \(p\in\mathcal P\), \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\), and \(N\ge N_0\), \(1\le\lceil Na(p)+\gamma\sqrt N\rceil\le N-1\).
statements.justification: The deterministic bound makes every finite-chain generator and staffing rule well-defined without hidden clipping.
statements.gap: The anchor invokes sufficiently large populations but does not state a compact-uniform enrollment threshold for the entire rate and staffing box.
statements.consumer: A certificate checker can reject infeasible enrollment values before evaluating the stochastic model.

statements.statement: For every fixed compact time interval, uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\), the stationary paths \(X_{0,N}\) and \(X_{1,N}\) converge in bounded-Lipschitz distance on Skorokhod space to the stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process \(X_0\) and stationary piecewise Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process \(X_\gamma\). For every \(f\in C_c^3(\mathbb R)\) and every fixed \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}<\infty\), the corresponding scaled generators satisfy \(\sup_{x\in E_{0,N}\cap[-R_{\mathrm{loc}},R_{\mathrm{loc}}]}|(G_{0,N}-\mathcal L_0)f(x)|+\sup_{x\in E_{1,N}\cap[-R_{\mathrm{loc}},R_{\mathrm{loc}}]}|(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N})f(x)|\to0\). Their invariant laws converge compact-uniformly to \(\pi_0\) and \(\pi_\gamma\), the Poisson construction uniquely determines centered solutions with \(1/D\le h_\gamma'(x)\le1/d\), and \(V_{0,N}\to V_0\), \(V_{1,N}\to V_\gamma\) uniformly.
statements.justification: This theorem relates the actual scaled finite generators and stationary paths to the two limiting diffusions and makes the long-run variance evaluable.
statements.gap: Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli give a fluid limit but no critical stationary path or Poisson-energy limit; Braverman and Dai study a different many-server system and a static-law metric.
statements.consumer: Trial planners can compute the capacity-dependent precision curve without simulating each large finite chain.

statements.statement: Can the lattice-residual handle prove a constant \(K_{\mathrm{res}}<\infty\), depending only on \((c,C,G)\), such that for every \(N\ge N_0\), on the scaled lattice \(E_{1,N}\), \[\sup_{p\in\mathcal P,\,|\gamma|\le G}\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}\left|\{G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N}\}h_{1,N}(X_{1,N})\right|\le K_{\mathrm{res}}N^{-1/2},\] including states whose upward or downward lattice jump crosses \(\gamma_N\)?
statements.justification: This is the early-kill bound that converts the scaled mean approximation into the order \(N^{-1}\) effect-centering error required by fitted inference.
statements.gap: Steady-state Stein results control static test functions, but no cited theorem gives this expected residual for the occupation Poisson solution at every ceiling phase and kink-crossing jump.
statements.consumer: A positive answer validates diffusion-fitted inference for Keheala-like trials; failure leaves exact-center empirical inference as the defensible fallback.

statements.statement: Over \(\mathcal M\), with no upper restriction on the relative growth of \(T_N\) and \(N\), uniformly in \((p,\gamma)\in\mathcal P\times[-G,G]\), \(\big(\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\theta_N),\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat p-p)^{\mathsf T}\big)^{\mathsf T}\) converges to a centered Gaussian vector with covariance \(\begin{pmatrix}V&A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma\\\Gamma A&\Gamma\end{pmatrix}\), and \(I_{\mathrm{emp}}\) covers \(\theta_N\) with probability \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly. This strictly strengthens Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli's fixed-\(N\), \(T\to\infty\) occupation theorem for the identical model by allowing system size and duration to diverge jointly and compact-uniformly in the critical staffing window.
statements.justification: The exact prelimit Poisson martingale removes the need to approximate trajectories over the growing horizon and yields the marked-score covariance on the joint array.
statements.gap: Boutilier et al. separate fixed-system sampling from fluid scaling; Wang and Plechac fix one CTMC and do not supply this critical finite-source covariance kernel.
statements.consumer: Investigators can analyze a critically loaded service trial using the dependence induced by shared capacity rather than participant-level independence.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fit}}\), \(\sqrt{NT_N}(\widetilde\theta_N-\theta_N)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,Q)\), \(\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\widetilde\theta_N)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,W)\), and \(I_{\mathrm{fit}}\) covers \(\theta_N\) with probability \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly. The fixed-implemented-staffing derivative is \(A=\nabla a_0-DH\nabla a\), so \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\) and \(W=V-A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\). The residual question gives \(O(N^{-1})\) effect-centering error; therefore \(T_N/N\to0\) is the weakest sufficient upper-growth relation furnished by that bound, because its normalized bias is \(O(\sqrt{T_N/N})\).
statements.justification: The theorem turns same-path rate fitting into an explicit fixed-capacity score projection and states exactly when the diffusion center is accurate enough.
statements.gap: Generic nuisance-score projection theory does not derive this model's fixed-staffing derivative, critical triangular-array law, or uniform center approximation.
statements.consumer: Keheala-like platforms can report implemented-effect intervals from the same marked transitions used to estimate behavioral rates.

statements.statement: Given the rational interval name \(\mathfrak r\) for \((p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G)\) and every rational \(\epsilon>0\), the Gaussian interval oracle constructs a rational \(L_J\) and the branch-and-bound algorithm returns \(\mathrm{Cert}\), \(\gamma_\epsilon\in[-G,G]\), and rational \(L_\epsilon,U_\epsilon\) satisfying \(L_\epsilon\le\min_{|\gamma|\le G}J(p,\gamma)\le J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)\le U_\epsilon\) and \(U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon\le\epsilon\). Every global minimizer lies in the certificate's unpruned interval cover, and every pruning decision is validated by an oracle lower bound. The full-level fallback terminates after at most \(2^{D_\epsilon+1}-1\) interval evaluations and fewer than \(3\cdot2^{D_\epsilon+1}\) interval-objective or point-oracle requests at precision at least \(m_\epsilon\); for \(G=0\), one certified point evaluation suffices.
statements.justification: The theorem gives finite certificate semantics and a worst-case termination bound even when the information objective is nonconvex or minimized at a boundary.
statements.gap: The anchor plots staffing choices without certified error; generic interval methods do not supply the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy oracle or its modulus.
statements.consumer: A sponsor receives a machine-checkable staffing recommendation and an explicit precision-adjusted optimality gap.

statements.statement: Uniformly for \(p\in\mathcal P\), the certified offset satisfies \(J_N(p,\gamma_\epsilon)-\inf_{|\gamma|\le G}J_N(p,\gamma)\le\epsilon+o(1)\).
statements.justification: A diffusion optimizer is operationally meaningful only if its certificate transfers to the actual integer-capacity experiment.
statements.gap: Borst, Mandelbaum, and Reiman prove recovery for an open-queue cost, not the finite-source inferential objective here.
statements.consumer: The staffing manager can implement \(M_N=\lceil Na+\gamma_\epsilon\sqrt N\rceil\) with asymptotically certified finite-system regret.

statements.statement: In the continuous extension \(\nu\downarrow0\), the treatment diffusion reduces to the control Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, \(m_\gamma\to0\), and \(V_\gamma\to2\lambda\tau/(\lambda+\tau)^3\). For fixed \(N\), the exact prelimit Poisson martingale reduces as \(T_N\to\infty\) to the fixed-system occupation central limit theorem of Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli.
statements.justification: These reductions prevent the critical construction from changing the known unconstrained and fixed-system limits.
statements.gap: They are fidelity checks rather than standalone novelty claims.
statements.consumer: Readers obtain regression tests against the closed-form control-arm and published fixed-system formulas.

sampling_model.design: Two equal-sized arms are randomized before monitoring; for every \(N\ge N_0\), the treatment arm receives the interior capacity \(M_N=\lceil Na+\gamma\sqrt N\rceil\), and the two aggregate arm processes evolve independently in stationarity.
sampling_model.units: Each arm contains \(N\) finite-source participants; dependence among treatment participants is induced by shared service capacity.
sampling_model.treatment: Control participants recover naturally at rate \(\tau\); treated participants additionally recover through service at aggregate rate \(\nu\min\{K_{1,N},M_N\}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Randomization identifies the implemented arm contrast; the model-based time-series law conditions on the realized equal arm sizes and capacity.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The primitive rates \((\lambda,\tau,\nu)\) are estimated from marked transition counts divided by their at-risk occupation exposures on the same two paths.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed finite arm sizes and staffing, the occupation contrast obeys a large-duration central limit theorem; separately, the many-system treatment effect has a deterministic fluid limit.
A piecewise Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusion approximates the stationary normalized system size in Wasserstein distance at order \(N^{-1/2}\) in its many-server model.
Prelimit Poisson equations can shift Stein-factor analysis from diffusion derivatives to finite differences for static steady-state approximation.
Mixing triangular arrays admit quantitative functional central limit bounds under stated moment and mixing conditions.
For a fixed countable-state CTMC, the Poisson martingale and likelihood-ratio score have a joint Brownian limit, and centered likelihood-ratio estimator variance is bounded in duration.
Estimating nuisance parameters by score equations can reduce the oracle sandwich variance by a score-projection term in regular estimating-equation models.
Square-root staffing is asymptotically optimal for an open call center under staffing and delay costs.
Queue-informed estimators and confidence intervals improve inference for stochastic-congestion experiments in an open single-server system.
Double machine learning yields efficient inference under conditional shared-state interference.

tldr: Capacity-constrained service trials sit where the published fixed-system central limit theorem and fluid approximation do not meet. The core proves compact-uniform stationary path, generator, Poisson-energy, and joint marked-score limits for the actual scaled finite chains; derives the fixed-implemented-staffing projection that changes fitted-center residual variance to \(V-A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\); and turns the piecewise-diffusion variance into a rationally certified capacity decision. Exact-center inference permits arbitrary joint divergence of \(N\) and \(T_N\), whereas fitted diffusion centering uses the derived weakest sufficient relation \(T_N=o(N)\). The load-bearing open question is the order \(N^{-1/2}\) expected residual \(\mathbb E|(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N})h_{1,N}|\) through the moving kink.

project_justification.gap: The operational-dosage literature provides a finite-system long-duration law and a separate fluid threshold, while its planning calculations assume oracle queueing quantities. Static steady-state diffusion approximation and fixed-chain score sensitivity do not close the joint critical inference problem.
project_justification.niche: A one-dimensional finite-source birth--death structure permits exact prelimit flux identities, yet the critical staffing kink makes fitted centering and variance design nontrivial. This creates a tractable but genuinely new bridge between experimental operational dosage, Markov additive-functional inference, and certified capacity choice.
project_justification.fill: The paper establishes stationary path and generator convergence for the named scaled lattices, proves the exact-centered joint Gaussian law without an artificial horizon exponent, isolates the kink residual needed for fitted intervals under \(T_N=o(N)\), and returns a rational interval certificate with explicit semantics and finite worst-case complexity.

related_work: Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli define the identical operational occupation effect and critical capacity scale, but their Theorem 1 fixes the finite system and their Theorem 2 is a separate fluid result; Theorem 2 here strictly joins population and duration divergence for their model. Braverman and Dai supply piecewise-diffusion Poisson and generator-comparison tools for static steady-state approximation, while Braverman's prelimit formulation informs the lattice residual route; neither is claimed as a theorem-level extension. Hafouta informs uniform triangular-array reasoning, although the exact Poisson martingale here removes any need for an arbitrary upper horizon exponent in exact-center inference. Wang and Plechac derive the fixed-CTMC score--Poisson mechanism adapted to marked rate estimation. Lok establishes generic score-projection variance subtraction, so novelty lies in the fixed-implemented-capacity derivative and critical finite-source realization. Borst, Mandelbaum, and Reiman inform square-root staffing recovery, while Corliss and Rall and Jansson and Knueppel provide the validated quadrature and branch-and-bound ingredients formalized here as a rational oracle. Li, Johari, Kuang, and Wager already establish queue-informed inference for an open stochastic-congestion system; this claim is confined to the closed finite-source critical window. Hays and Raghavan address general shared-state interference but do not derive this primitive CTMC limit or capacity certificate.
technical_internal_limitation: The numerical witness \((\lambda,\tau,\nu,\gamma)=(1,1,1,0)\) gives floating-point values \(V=0.4804862942\) and \(W=0.4076427604\), but these remain diagnostics rather than certified theorem outputs. The rational interval oracle is a mathematical specification, not an implemented library. Marked recovery causes, stationary initialization, independent arms, compactly positive rates, and a bounded staffing window are substantive restrictions. The fitted-center theorem must be dropped if the uniform kink-residual question fails, although exact-center empirical inference and the exact Poisson-martingale law may remain viable.
honest_scope: The exact birth--death flux representation, limiting density, score-covariance algebra, and explicit interior threshold provide strong traction but are not treated as proved. The principal open content is the compact-uniform residual bound on the scaled treatment lattice and its order \(N^{-1}\) effect-centering consequence. Exact-center joint inference requires only \(N,T_N\to\infty\); the additional operational regime \(T_N=o(N)\) is imposed only for diffusion-fitted centering because the available center remainder becomes \(O(\sqrt{T_N/N})\) after normalization. The proposal does not claim randomization inference after assignment, efficiency under unmarked histories, robustness to common shocks, arbitrary initialization, heterogeneous risk classes, or a clinical cure effect.

seed_details.anchor: BoutilierJonassonLiYoeli2024, Theorems 1 and 2 and Appendix B.1
seed_details.opportunity: Unify the anchor's fixed-system duration limit and deterministic large-system limit at square-root staffing by a compact-uniform triangular-array occupation CLT with a piecewise Ornstein--Uhlenbeck variance kernel.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's fixed-state-space ergodic CLT invocation by an exact prelimit Poisson martingale and prove convergence of its stationary energy across the moving staffing kink.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-source occupation CLTs, piecewise Ornstein--Uhlenbeck occupation limits, and critical service-experiment inference located steady-state approximation and generic triangular-array results, but no theorem for this target--method pair.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from the anchor's finite-state CLT and fluid limit by interchanging limits.
seed_details.rebuttal: The anchor fixes \(N\) in its CLT and its fluid model is deterministic; neither controls the Green--Kubo variance or the \(N^{-1}\) centering error uniformly at the critical kink.

seed_details.anchor: BoutilierJonassonLiYoeli2024, Appendix D.2 and WangPlechac2019, Theorems 4.1--4.2
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the joint law of the occupation contrast and marked-count rate estimates and show that fitting the diffusion center on the same trajectory leaves residual variance \(V-A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\), with \(A\) differentiated at fixed implemented staffing.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Augment the Poisson martingale by the three marked counting-process scores and differentiate the critical coordinate while holding the observed integer capacity fixed.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for fixed-staffing score correction and fitted-center queueing experiments located CTMC likelihood-ratio sensitivity, but not a many-system same-path projection identity.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a routine delta method once primitive rates are estimated.
seed_details.rebuttal: A routine independent plug-in gives the wrong sign and magnitude because the center and contrast share jump martingales; the fixed-capacity derivative changes \(A\), and the covariance projection must be derived from event marks.

seed_details.opportunity: Choose the square-root staffing offset by minimizing an interval-width objective whose variance is an implicit piecewise-diffusion Poisson energy, with a terminating interval certificate and finite-system regret transfer.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace numerical selection of the staffing offset by rigorous quadrature enclosures and a uniform objective approximation supporting branch-and-bound and a recovery sequence.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for critical-diffusion experimental capacity optimization found classical queue-cost staffing and generic interval optimization, but not an information-variance staffing objective for a finite-source trial.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is merely a one-dimensional grid search around a classical square-root staffing rule.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objective contains a kinked Poisson-energy integral and can have boundary or multiple optima; the claimed object is a proof-carrying global certificate plus uniform finite-system regret, not a plotted heuristic.

seed_details.opportunity: Jointly choose class priority and staffing while deriving policy-value inference for risk-weighted occupation outcomes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Prove state-space collapse for class occupancies under priority service before any scalar Poisson argument can begin.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found personalized allocation and multidimensional piecewise-diffusion tools separately, but no critical-load policy-value law for this finite-source system.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Priority classes are an obvious multitype extension of the homogeneous birth--death chain.
seed_details.rebuttal: Total occupancy ceases to be lumpable, so the scalar stationary product and Poisson solution disappear; a new collapse theorem is indispensable.

seed_details.opportunity: Design randomization when treated and control participants share one service pool, identify the global all-treated contrast, and derive critical-diffusion coverage.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace independent treatment and control chains by an assignment-indexed joint occupancy process and derive an exposure map or state-space collapse.
seed_details.destination_search: The search located mean-field marketplace bias and dynamic-interference consistency, but no design-based critical law for a closed service pool.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Standard exposure-mapping inference already covers shared capacity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Queue-generated exposures are endogenous, persistent, and assignment-dependent; fixed network exposure probabilities do not yield the required global-effect identification or diffusion limit.

seed_details.opportunity: Replace cumulative occupation by the stationary rate of undesirable episodes exceeding a clinically relevant duration and derive its critical limit law.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift the count chain to an age-augmented Markov process because the path-pattern functional is not measurable from occupancy alone.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor names sustained histories as omitted; bounded searches found occupation-time methods but no finite-source critical episode-duration inference for service trials.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a routine change of the reward function in an additive-functional CLT.
seed_details.rebuttal: Duration exceedance is not a function of the scalar occupancy state and requires an age-measure state and a different critical limit.

seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the efficiency bound and an attaining estimator when natural and service recoveries are observationally unmarked.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project the complete-data marked score onto the filtration generated only by aggregate up and down jumps.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches located general partially observed CTMC estimation but no efficiency calculation for this critically staffed finite-source contrast.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The unmarked likelihood is obtained by simply adding the two death intensities.
seed_details.rebuttal: Although the observed intensity is easy to write, separating \(\tau\) and \(\nu\) and deriving the efficient influence function under critical scaling is not supplied by the complete-data score.

seed_details.opportunity: Allow staffing to update in batches from accruing marked histories and construct martingale-valid inference under the induced adaptive filtration.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a stationary generator by a predictable sequence of generators and stabilize the occupation-score martingale across staffing updates.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found adaptive-experiment martingale inference and queue staffing separately, but no capacity-adaptive operational-effect interval in the critical window.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Batched adaptive inference follows directly from standard martingale central limit theorems.
seed_details.rebuttal: Changing capacity changes the estimand and invariant law, so a stabilized martingale alone does not control adaptive target drift.

seed_details.opportunity: Permit slowly drifting primitive rates and obtain a local-stationary occupation law with a time-integrated critical variance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace stationarity by blockwise frozen generators and control the accumulated Poisson remainder between adjacent blocks.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found nonstationary congestion inference and mixing triangular arrays, but no finite-source kinked critical diffusion with time-varying rates.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Slow variation is a routine blocking argument applied to the stationary theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The staffing threshold and stationary center move with the rates, creating a first-order tracking bias that must be separated from mixing error.

seed_details.opportunity: Choose enrollment, duration, and integer capacity jointly to minimize cost subject to uniform power, with a diffusion lower bound and an integer recovery sequence.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive a uniform power approximation over two diverging design coordinates before adapting the staffing lower-bound and recovery-sequence argument.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor numerically chooses enrollment and capacity; classical dimensioning optimizes service cost rather than causal power, leaving the joint inferential design pair unoccupied.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is the anchor's power program with a diffusion approximation inserted.
seed_details.rebuttal: The anchor assumes oracle queue parameters and offers no uniform approximation, lower bound, or recovery sequence certifying optimal integer designs.

literature_map.settled: Theorem 1 gives a \(T\to\infty\) central limit theorem at fixed finite capacity and population; Theorem 2 gives a separate deterministic fluid treatment effect; Appendix D.2 uses oracle primitive quantities and leaves their estimation open.
literature_map.unsettled: No joint \(N,T_N\to\infty\) critical-window occupation law, same-path rate-score correction, or certified choice of \(\gamma\) is supplied.
literature_map.key_location: Introduction, Sections 2.2--2.3, Theorems 1--2, Appendix B.1, Appendix D.2--D.3, and Conclusion of arXiv version 3.

literature_map.settled: Poisson equations, Stein-factor bounds, generator coupling, and stationary moments yield order \(N^{-1/2}\) static steady-state approximation, including piecewise drift; the prelimit variant replaces diffusion derivatives by finite differences.
literature_map.unsettled: These papers do not approximate the growing-horizon occupation energy, its marked-score cross-brackets, or the fixed-staffing fitted center.
literature_map.key_location: Braverman and Dai's main Wasserstein theorem and proof architecture; Braverman's Introduction and Sections 3--4 on prelimit generator comparison.

literature_map.settled: Quantitative functional central limit bounds are available for mixing triangular arrays and contracting Markov chains under moment and contraction controls.
literature_map.unsettled: Those generic results do not establish the finite-source stationary approximation, kink-crossing residual, or explicit Poisson variance. The exact prelimit martingale route here yields exact-center inference for arbitrary joint divergence, so no borrowed polynomial horizon ceiling is imposed.
literature_map.key_location: Introduction and the contracting-Markov-chain applications in Section 3.

literature_map.settled: Theorems 4.1--4.2 give a joint fixed-chain Brownian limit for a Poisson martingale and a likelihood-ratio score; Theorems 5.1--5.2 bound centered likelihood-ratio variance uniformly in duration.
literature_map.unsettled: The paper does not study marked-count maximum likelihood estimators jointly with a many-system critical occupation contrast or differentiate a center at fixed realized capacity.

literature_map.settled: Queue-aware estimators and confidence intervals exist for open single-server stochastic congestion, and efficient double-machine-learning inference exists under conditional shared-state interference.
literature_map.unsettled: Neither congestion source supplies the closed finite-source critical-window variance kernel, marked-rate projection, or capacity certificate in this proposal. Lok's score-projection theorem shows that variance subtraction itself is classical, so novelty must reside in the model-specific joint law and fixed-implemented-capacity derivative.
literature_map.key_location: Li et al. abstract and model overview; Hays and Raghavan abstract and main shared-state inference theorem; Lok Sections 5.4--5.7 and equations (20)--(30).

literature_map.settled: Square-root staffing can be asymptotically optimal for open call-center cost objectives; interval quadrature and derivative-free interval branch-and-bound provide verified enclosures and global-minimum certificates.
literature_map.unsettled: No cited result supplies a rational interval oracle for this finite-source piecewise-diffusion Poisson energy, a certified modulus, explicit certificate semantics, and the resulting finite branch-and-bound complexity.
literature_map.key_location: Borst et al. limiting-cost and recovery argument; Corliss and Rall's adaptive validation construction; Jansson and Knueppel's inclusion-function branch-and-bound theorem.

novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level result is Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli's fixed-\(N\), large-duration occupation central limit theorem paired with a separate deterministic fluid limit. The proposed kernel strictly joins these axes in the square-root staffing window using the actual scaled finite generators, stationary path limits, Poisson energies, and a compact-uniform marked-score law. The exact-centered theorem needs no upper relation between duration and population. The fitted-center result separately uses the fixed-implemented-capacity derivative and the weakest relation justified by the order \(N^{-1}\) effect-center error, namely \(T_N=o(N)\). Wang and Plechac and Lok inform the score algebra but do not provide this derivative or triangular-array realization. Braverman and Dai inform the residual architecture but not the growing-horizon occupation law. The capacity theorem adds a rational Gaussian-tail and quadrature oracle, checkable pruning semantics, and a finite complexity bound tied to the new variance kernel rather than classical open-queue delay cost.
